tools.summary: Tools are the model-controlled primitive: the server describes each one with a name, a description and a JSON Schema for its arguments, and the client calls it with `tools/call`. Know the exact result shape (content blocks, `structuredContent`, `isError`), the two error channels, why annotations are only hints, and how to design a small, well-described tool surface that a model can use without drowning its context.
points: A tool definition has a required `name` and `inputSchema`, plus optional `title`, `description`, `icons`, `outputSchema` and `annotations`. Display-name precedence is `title`, then `annotations.title`, then `name`.

`inputSchema` MUST be a valid JSON Schema object (never `null`) with `type: "object"` at the root; any JSON Schema 2020-12 keyword is allowed (2026-07-28 loosened this). With no `$schema` the dialect is 2020-12. For a tool with no parameters the recommended schema is `{ "type": "object", "additionalProperties": false }`.

Tool names SHOULD be 1 to 128 characters, case-sensitive, unique within a server, and use only ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`. Aggregating hosts SHOULD disambiguate collisions with their own prefix; `serverInfo.name` is not guaranteed unique.

Results carry a `content` array of blocks (`text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource_link`, embedded `resource`), optional `structuredContent` and optional `isError` (absent means false), plus `resultType: "complete"` in 2026-07-28. Linked resources need not appear in `resources/list`.

If `outputSchema` is declared, servers MUST return conforming `structuredContent` and clients SHOULD validate it. A tool returning structured content SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a text block for older clients. `structuredContent` may now be any JSON value, including an array.

Two error channels: protocol errors (unknown tool, request failing the `CallToolRequest` schema, server failures) are JSON-RPC errors, for example `-32602` for an unknown tool. Tool execution errors (API failures, bad values such as a past date or wrong date format, business rules) are results with `isError: true` and an actionable message. Clients SHOULD pass execution errors to the model; protocol errors only MAY be passed.

Annotations `readOnlyHint` (default false), `destructiveHint` (default true), `idempotentHint` (default false) and `openWorldHint` (default true) are hints. `destructiveHint` and `idempotentHint` only matter when `readOnlyHint` is false. Clients MUST treat annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted.

`tools/list` MUST NOT vary per connection or as a side effect of other requests, but MAY vary by the authorization on the request. Servers SHOULD return a deterministic order for client caching and prompt-cache hits; results carry `ttlMs` and `cacheScope`, and `listChanged` servers send `notifications/tools/list_changed` to clients listening with `toolsListChanged: true`.

No protocol sessions: cross-call state uses an explicit, opaque, server-minted handle returned by a creation tool and passed back as an argument. Check the caller's authorization against the handle every call, state the lifetime in the description, and return an `isError` result for expired handles.
A broken Streamable HTTP stream means the client re-issues the call as a new request with a new id, so side-effecting tools need their own idempotency keys.

Server MUSTs: validate all inputs, enforce access control, rate limit, sanitize outputs. Client SHOULDs: confirm sensitive operations, show inputs before calling, validate results, set timeouts, log usage, never auto-fetch network `$ref`s (reject unresolvable ones) and bound the cost of composition-heavy schemas.

Design for the model: a few workflow-level tools rather than one per endpoint, descriptions written for a new colleague, unambiguous parameter names (`user_id`), enums for closed sets, high-signal and bounded responses (pagination, filtering, a `response_format` choice), actionable error text, and evaluations with realistic tasks and held-out sets.
traps: Returning a JSON-RPC error for a fixable input problem: the model may never see it. Use `isError: true` with a message that says how to fix the call.
Treating `readOnlyHint: true` from an arbitrary server as permission to auto-run a tool; annotations are untrusted hints and never replace authorization.
Assuming an omitted `destructiveHint` means safe: it defaults to `true`, and `openWorldHint` defaults to `true` too.
Writing `"required": true` inside a property; in 2020-12 `required` is an array on the parent object, and the boolean form fails meta-schema validation.
Deduplicating retries on the JSON-RPC id, or keeping state under `Mcp-Session-Id`: re-issued calls get new ids, and sessions no longer exist in 2026-07-28.
Unlocking extra tools after a `login` call on the same connection; lists may vary by request credentials, not by earlier requests.
Using `tools/list` pagination to shrink huge tool outputs; protocol pagination is for list operations, so tools must page or truncate their own results.
